feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. What I had to do in the controller: nothing beyond the iteration 7 gains (kp 0.8, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction). I kept them because iteration 7 is the only measured controller for this geometry, and every gain change I could make on this geometry is untested. Evidence: iteration 7 (80 mm row, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 1.0 kg) scored 73.33, the best so far. Mass 1.2 kg (iteration 8) fell to 60.14, and wheel radius 0.035 m (iteration 9, with kp 0.7) fell to 64.78, so those levers have turned over near the current values. Iteration 10 (0.025 m wheels, kp 0.96) scored 72.71, close to iteration 7, which suggests the radius-to-gain match is roughly neutral in that direction. Max error sat at 0.060 to 0.067 m on every track while RMS stayed at 0.019 to 0.036 m, so the peak is a bend transient. Decision rules for the next race (no further iteration will follow, so these are for the record): if the race reports line_loss_events of 2 on the slalom, the 12 mm footprint is losing the line and a 16 mm sensor would be the next test. If max_error on the unseen track stays above 0.06 m with steering_oscillation near 0.17, the peak is bend overshoot, and a kd change (about 0.18) would be the next test. If the race finishes with progress well below 0.5, the speed limit is the issue, and wheel_radius 0.025 m with kp 0.96 is the next test.
requested_changes: Test sensor_size 0.016 m on the 80 mm row with everything else unchanged. The slalom shows 2.0 line-loss events in iterations 0, 3 to 7 and 9 to 10, and a larger footprint keeps readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold for longer. Iteration 1 changed sensor size with other variables, so this is not yet proven.

Test wheel_radius 0.025 m with kp 0.96 and everything else unchanged. Iteration 10 scored 72.71 against 73.33, and the bend-versus-straight trade-off is still open. Iteration 9 (0.035 m) raised oval progress from 0.227 to 0.273 but cut s-bend progress from 0.194 to 0.078.

Test mass 1.1 kg with everything else unchanged. Mass peaked near 1.0 kg (0.6 kg gave 55.4, 1.0 kg gave 73.3, 1.2 kg gave 60.1), so 1.1 kg is a narrow test of whether the optimum sits slightly above 1.0 kg.
